name: Galgar
summary: Near the Den in the Valley of Trials, Galgar feeds young Horde recruits. He asks newcomers to gather wild cactus apples for his Cactus Apple Surprise.

sections.title: A Cook in the Valley
sections.body: Galgar cooks by the Den's fire in the Valley of Trials. He feeds young orcs and trolls through their first rites of passage. Durotar is a dry, harsh red wasteland, so food must be found across the land. Galgar sends novice warriors to gather ripe cactus fruit, testing their attention and resilience while stocking his kitchen.

sections.title: Cactus Apple Surprise
sections.body: Galgar calls his specialty Cactus Apple Surprise. He says gathering spiny desert fruit is a simple way to ease fresh recruits into adventuring. The dish still feeds hungry trainees. Every Horde warrior begins somewhere, and Galgar starts them by foraging in the desert.

faq.answer: Galgar is near the central campfire and cooking area outside the Den, in the Valley of Trials. The canyon lies in southwestern Durotar and is where orcs and trolls begin.

faq.q: What does Galgar ask adventurers to do?
faq.answer: Galgar asks new adventurers to gather ripe cactus apples from wild cacti scattered across the Valley of Trials. He uses them to prepare his Cactus Apple Surprise.

faq.q: Why does Galgar send new recruits to pick fruit?
faq.answer: Galgar says the task is simple. It gives fledgling fighters an early chore to learn the valley and practice self-sufficiency in Durotar's harsh wilderness.
Cactus Apple Surprise is Galgar's signature recipe. He makes it with fresh cactus apples gathered from Durotar's native desert plants to feed novice recruits.

angles.text: Galgar cooks in the Horde's practical, rustic way. He uses Durotar's sparse natural resources to feed recruits and keep them ready for battle.
As a young orc in the Valley of Trials, you gather fruit for Galgar as a familiar rite of passage before facing fiercer wilderness threats.
